title: Fetch quotes concurrently
problem: fetch_quotes asks a slow async API for one stock quote per symbol, but awaits each lookup before starting the next, so 4 symbols take 4 round trips. Make the lookups run concurrently while keeping the result in input order and fetching each distinct symbol only once.
requirements: All distinct symbols are looked up concurrently (with 4 distinct symbols, all 4 lookups are in flight at once)
The result dict is keyed in first-seen input order, not in the order lookups finish
Each distinct symbol is fetched exactly once
fetch_quotes stays async def and awaits get_quote's coroutines (no threads)
contract: async def fetch_quotes(symbols: list[str], get_quote: Callable[[str], Awaitable[float]]) -> dict[str, float]
expectedBehavior: fetch_quotes(['SLOW', 'FAST', 'MID'], api) returns a dict whose keys are ['SLOW', 'FAST', 'MID'] even though FAST finishes first, in about the time of the slowest lookup.
edgeCases: Duplicates (IBM, IBM, SAP, IBM): 2 calls, keys ['IBM', 'SAP']
Lookups that finish in a different order than they started
hints: Conceptual: awaiting coroutines one by one is sequential. To overlap the waits, hand all of them to the event loop first, then wait for all of them together.
Specific: remove duplicates while keeping order (dict.fromkeys does that), then start one task per symbol inside an asyncio.TaskGroup, or pass all coroutines to asyncio.gather.

Implementation: with a TaskGroup, keep a dict {symbol: tg.create_task(get_quote(symbol))}; after the async with block ends, build the result from each task's .result(). With gather, zip the unique symbols with the returned list.
evaluation: Results are matched to symbols by position or by key, never by completion order
No sequential await inside the loop
The learner can explain why `await asyncio.gather(...)` returns results in argument order
